title: BCCI Plans FTP Overhaul After Overseas Collapses and Mounting Injury Crisis
excerpt: After series defeats in Ireland and England and a wave of player injuries, the BCCI will push for rest periods and acclimatisation windows before future SENA tours in the next scheduling cycle.
body:
• The BCCI held a review meeting on September 3 in Mumbai with captains Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer, head coach Gautam Gambhir, and CoE head VVS Laxman to address India's overseas struggles and mounting injury crisis
  • BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia said the board will push for the next FTP to include adequate rest periods and acclimatisation windows before tours to SENA countries
  • India lost T20I series in both Ireland (2-0) and England (4-0) and went down 2-1 in the ODI series in England, with multiple players breaking down mid-tour after the IPL
  • Key injuries hit Jasprit Bumrah, Hardik Pandya, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Harshit Rana, and Washington Sundar during the England assignment

The Board of Control for Cricket in India held a review meeting at its Mumbai headquarters on September 3 to assess the national team's recent run of overseas defeats and a growing injury list, with BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia acknowledging that the board needs to restructure future scheduling to protect player welfare.

The meeting brought together Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, head coach Gautam Gambhir, and Centre of Excellence head VVS Laxman alongside top BCCI officials. The agenda centered on what Saikia described as "soul-searching" after India's poor showings on back-to-back overseas assignments.

The Losses That Forced the Rethink

India suffered a 2-0 T20I series defeat in Ireland, followed by a 4-0 whitewash in the T20I series in England. The team also went down 2-1 in the ODI series in England, a result that particularly stung given the squad depth available.

"Yes, we did not do well," Saikia told reporters after the meeting, according to ANI. "We wanted to know what the reasons are. We have to do certain soul-searching about that."

Injury Crisis Compounds the Problem

The results were made worse by a cascade of injuries that thinned the squad mid-tour. Jasprit Bumrah could not get through a three-match series without breaking down. Hardik Pandya, already managing a back issue, picked up a quadriceps strain during rehab at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence. His replacement, Nitish Kumar Reddy, also went down with a quad injury. Harshit Rana and Washington Sundar suffered hamstring problems at various points during the tour, according to Sporting News.

Saikia pointed to the punishing schedule as the root cause. "If you look at England, we have a team of 15 players who went for the ODI, and out of those 15, three or four players got injured," he said. "We have to think that they had played two months of IPL before that. So all this takes a toll."

FTP Overhaul Planned

The BCCI's solution targets the structural level. Saikia said the board's representatives at upcoming international scheduling forums would push for the next Future Tours Programme cycle to build in proper rest windows and acclimatisation time, including practice matches, before major tours to SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand, and Australia.

"In the next FTP, we will ensure proper rest for the players, acclimatisation, or some practice matches before any major series in SENA countries."

— Devajit Saikia, BCCI Secretary

The number of matches may also be reduced in the next cycle, according to SportsTak. The BCCI is also taking feedback from captains and coaching staff to develop rehab protocols that ensure injured players return to international cricket through a structured pathway rather than being rushed back.

CoE Vacancy and Upcoming Schedule

The position of Head of Sports Science at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru remains vacant, though Saikia said operations are not hampered, with 16 specialists currently managing fitness, rehabilitation, and prehab programs. A fresh global search has been announced.

India faces a packed schedule for the rest of 2026: a three-match T20I series against Afghanistan starting September 13, the West Indies tour with three ODIs and five T20Is through October, the Asian Games T20 tournament in Japan, and a lengthy tour of New Zealand from late October through December featuring five T20Is, five ODIs, and two Tests — exactly the kind of SENA assignment Saikia flagged as needing better preparation.

For Indian cricket fans globally, the review signals that the BCCI is taking the workload problem seriously at a systemic level rather than treating injuries as isolated incidents. Whether that translates into meaningful schedule changes depends on negotiations at the ICC's international planning forums, where India's influence is considerable but not absolute.
nri_angle: Indian cricket fans globally are watching whether the BCCI's promised scheduling changes will better protect player welfare ahead of high-stakes overseas tours.
author: Diaspora Desk
